basic_info.title: SQ-VAE: Variational Bayes on Discrete Representation with Self-annealed Stochastic Quantization

method.training_signal: variational (Gaussian dequantization/quantization with a learned, ANNEALING variance instead of a fixed free-bits/commitment hinge)
method.notes: Diagnoses standard VQ-VAE codebook collapse as a consequence of ad hoc training heuristics (straight-through estimator + commitment loss + EMA updates), and replaces them with a single principled variational objective in which quantization is STOCHASTIC (soft assignment) early in training and 'self-anneals' toward deterministic hard quantization as training progresses -- the variance/temperature of the quantization noise is itself a learned parameter that shrinks automatically, rather than a hand-scheduled or fixed hyperparameter. This is the clearest available precedent for '(b) an adaptive/scheduled alternative to a FIXED threshold' in a categorical/discrete-latent bottleneck: instead of a fixed 1-nat-per-group free-bits floor, an analogous self-annealed scheme would let the effective free-bits floor per group start loose (encouraging exploration/ use of many groups) and tighten (or loosen, symmetrically) based on a learned per-group scale rather than a global constant. Adapting this cheaply to the exact setup (straight-through categorical RSSM, unimix already present) would mean: replace the fixed free-bits scalar with a per-group learned temperature/scale that is optimized jointly (e.g. via a small auxiliary loss term keeping it well-behaved), NOT changing model capacity, NOT requiring new data. This is the single most literature-grounded 'adaptive free bits' mechanism found, though the paper's own instantiation is for Gaussian-based dequantization, not softmax-categorical straight-through, so the categorical-group version would need a first-principles re-derivation rather than a direct port.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Not a map-matching or RL paper -- a discrete-bottleneck-training-methodology precedent for literature gap (b), adaptive/scheduled free-bits alternatives, requested 2026-07-26.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Directly answers the literature-gap question 'is there post-hoc/adaptive free-bits work' with the closest documented mechanism (self-annealing variance in place of a fixed KL/commitment floor), predating DreamerV3 but addressing exactly the class of fixed-floor problem DreamerV3's free bits also has.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Not BMW-relevant; logged as the strongest candidate mechanism for an adaptive-free-bits experiment on the categorical RSSM if the pseudo-label signal-ceiling fix (higher literature priority) does not resolve kl_act pinning.

uncertain: No published adaptation of SQ-VAE's self-annealing mechanism to a DreamerV3-style straight-through categorical RSSM (with KL balancing + unimix) was found as of this search -- this would be a novel combination, not an off-the-shelf technique to import.
